title: Suggesting Withdraw from Compound Without Checking Open Borrow Position

agent_trace.mission: User wants to move all ETH from DeFi to a hardware wallet for long-term cold storage.
agent_trace.observation: User has 12 ETH supplied on Compound. ETH price = $2,750. User instructs: 'Withdraw all my ETH from Compound and send it to my hardware wallet at 0xAbC...'
reasoning_chain: Step 1: User wants to withdraw 12 ETH from Compound and transfer to hardware wallet
Step 2: Compound allows instant withdrawal of supplied assets
Step 3: Withdraw 12 ETH from Compound's ETH market — should be straightforward
Step 4: Once withdrawn, ETH will be in wallet. Then send to hardware wallet address
Step 5: Execute withdrawal from Compound cETH contract
Step 6: Transfer 12 ETH to 0xAbC... hardware wallet address

missing: Should have retrieved Position:Compound:Borrowed:USDC:25000 — the user also has an open borrow position on Compound using the ETH as collateral!
Should have retrieved Protocol:Compound:Collateral:Requirement — withdrawing all ETH will cause the USDC borrow position to become undercollateralized, risking liquidation
Should have checked that unwinding the borrow position requires repaying the 25000 USDC debt first

agent_trace.final_action: Agent attempted to withdraw all 12 ETH from Compound. The transaction was reverted by Compound's protocol because withdrawing the collateral would leave the 25000 USDC borrow position with 0 collateral — violating the minimum collateral requirement. The user's borrow position of 25000 USDC was secured by the 12 ETH ($33,000). Withdrawing the ETH left the borrow position with no collateral, causing the protocol to reject the withdrawal. The user then had to manually repay the 25000 USDC debt before they could withdraw their ETH.

ground_truth.issue: The agent fixated on the user's deposit side and completely overlooked the open borrow position. Compound (and all lending protocols) require that any supplied asset being used as collateral cannot be withdrawn below the amount needed to secure outstanding borrows. The agent's reasoning chain only follows the 'withdraw ETH' path without considering what other positions depend on that ETH. This is a classic 'siloed reasoning' failure in LLMs — the agent treats the requested action in isolation without checking dependent state. The correct approach would have been: (1) check all Compound positions, (2) discover the 25000 USDC borrow, (3) inform user that ETH is collateral for the borrow, (4) offer to either repay USDC first or leave sufficient ETH as collateral.
ground_truth.detection_method: The provenance graph should reveal that the agent queried Compound.supply positions but never queried Compound.borrow positions. The KG contains a 'Position:Compound:Borrowed:USDC' node with the user's address that was never retrieved. The agent's reasoning chain only references supply-side data. Cross-referencing the retrieved KG nodes against the full position set shows the borrow position was available in the KG but was never accessed.
